task: Write one sentence of your own using the word amiable. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know amiable should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The amiable crossing guard has a kind word for every student, and even motorists stuck at her stop sign end up smiling.
Pleasant is milder than amiable — a pleasant clerk gives you no reason to complain, while an amiable one leaves you in a better mood than he found you.
Delightful goes further than amiable — delightful company is a highlight you talk about afterward, while amiable good nature is steady, comfortable, and everyday.

Good-natured describes a kindly, even temperament — someone slow to anger and quick to help. Amiable covers that kindness and adds pleasantness as company: an amiable person is not just kind inside but easy and agreeable to be around. Good-natured points at disposition; amiable points at how the company feels.

Likable only says people take to someone, for any reason at all — talent, humor, good looks. Amiable names one particular reason: a steady, pleasant good nature that makes a person easy company. A brilliant but prickly performer can be likable; amiable requires the warmth.

The corner barbershop had gone through three owners in five years, and each had left it a little emptier than the last.
He was not the fastest barber in town, and he never advertised.
What he had was an amiable way about him: he remembered names, asked after report cards and knee surgeries, and laughed easily at even the oldest jokes.
Customers began arriving early just to sit in the waiting chairs and talk.
Some came on days they needed no haircut at all.
Within a year the shop was full again — not because the cuts had changed, but because an hour with Ray left people feeling lighter than when they walked in.
